title: Why Agentic AI Is Not Yet FDA Approved
Predicting pandemics, predicting people: the ethical limits of AI-powered public health surveillance.
desc: [Frontiers in public health] Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming public health surveillance by enabling the integration of epidemiological, clinical, environmental, mobility, genomic, and digital data to detect emerging threats and anticipate disease transmission. However, the expansion from detecting outbreaks to predicting individual or group-level behaviors raises important ethical concerns related to privacy, autonomy, discrimination, transparency, accountability, and public trust. This mini-review examines the ethical limits of AI-powered public health surveillance, with particular attention to the transition from population-level epidemic prediction toward individual-level inference and profiling. It highlights how extensive data integration, algorithmic bias, unequal predictive errors, opaque models, and mission creep can undermine both equity and the legitimacy of surveillance systems. The review argues that predictive capability alone cannot establish ethical legitimacy. Instead, AI surveillance should be governed by necessity, proportionality, purpose limitation, data minimization, equity, transparency, meaningful human oversight, and mechanisms for accountability and redress. A lifecycle governance approach is further required to ensure continuous assessment of data quality, subgroup performance, model drift, unintended harms, and changing public-health needs. Ultimately, the ethical boundary of AI surveillance should be defined not by what can technically be predicted, but by what can be predicted and acted upon without compromising fundamental rights, equity, and public trust.

title: Beyond Physical Illness: Can Clinical Narratives Reveal Emerging Mental Health Risks in Chronically Ill Patients?
desc: Mental-health risks such as depression, dementia, and suicidal ideation can emerge during hospitalization among chronically ill patients and may worsen without timely recognition and intervention. However, most existing mental health studies focus on patients with established psychiatric conditions rather than patients hospitalized primarily for physical illness. In this work, we investigate whether latent mental-health risk in chronically ill patients can be inferred from longitudinal clinical narratives. We construct a weakly supervised cohort around 4,000 patients from MIMIC-III using mental-health evidence extracted from discharge summaries. A hierarchical state-space framework derives mental-health representations from day-wise clinical narratives and models their temporal evolution for risk estimation throughout hospitalization. Preliminary results demonstrate improved binary risk prediction using the proposed representations and show distinct model derived risk trajectories between risk and no-risk cohorts, providing a foundation for studying emerging mental-health risks in chronically ill patients.

title: Mimic: A Unified Neural Network Architecture for Modelling Genomic Sequences and Module-level Comparison
desc: There exist a wide range of Neural Networks (NNs) that have modelled genomic sequences well. The architectures of these NNs consist of three steps: k-mer embedding, sequence embedding, and output mapping. The NNs are primarily differentiated from one another by their sequence embedding components. Although different NNs have been compared before, these comparisons are often either limited or involve drastically different NNs. Another issue is that some NNs are configured for a specific sequence length, and different length sequences require manual modification of the architectures. This study examines the architectures of established NNs for genomics sequences. Based on these architectures, a novel NN called Mimic is developed that provides a unified architecture for the principled comparison of NN components. Mimic was used to model two different types of genomic datasets: protein-DNA interactions and enhancer activity. Along with other architecture components, different sequence embedding strategies were tried such as recurrent layers and convolutional layers. It was found that there exist specific NN components that yield significantly better performing models. Furthermore, Mimic significantly outperformed prevailing standard NNs, Bichrom and DeepSTARR, in modelling protein-DNA interactions and enhancer activity, respectively. This study provides a framework for more extensive studies toward a general prescription of NN architecture for modelling genomics data.

title: Monebo and Innolitics Secure FDA 510(k) Clearance for a Cross-Platform ECG Arrhythmia Analysis Library
Artificial intelligence and machine learning for magnetic nanoparticles and nanocarriers in cancer imaging, drug delivery, and magnetic control: a systematic review.
desc: [Beilstein journal of nanotechnology] We reviewed artificial intelligence and machine learning in magnetic resonance imaging-visible magnetic nanoparticles, nanocarriers, and systems for imaging, drug delivery, hyperthermia, targeting, transport, and control. Using "preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses (PRISMA) 2020" methods, 2,283 records from seven databases yielded 65 studies. Predicted outcomes were colloidal stability, toxicity, uptake, magnetic descriptors, specific absorption rate, relaxivity, MRI signal, superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticle (SPION) quantification, drug release, biodistribution, and magnetic navigation. Evidence was strongest in bounded tasks: magnetic-property and relaxivity prediction, image-derived SPION mapping, hyperthermia modelling, and controlled magnetic transport. Most studies optimised isolated endpoints rather than integrating stability, MRI visibility, drug loading, release, tumour delivery, safety, and therapeutic response. External validation across datasets, laboratories, particle batches, biological models, scanners, and patient cohorts remains limited.

title: OneEEG: A Unified Signal-Visual Multimodal Language Model with Task-Aware Mixture of Projectors for Multi-Task EEG Understanding
desc: Electroencephalography (EEG) is widely used in clinical assessment, brain-computer interfaces, and cognitive-state analysis, yet EEG modeling remains fragmented across task paradigms. Recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) provide a promising interface for flexible multimodal reasoning, but their ability to understand EEG inputs remains limited. In this work, we propose OneEEG, a unified EEG-MLLM framework for multi-task EEG understanding. By training on our curated OneEEG-Instruct, a multi-task EEG instruction-tuning dataset, OneEEG jointly models numerical EEG representations and visual EEG representations, and introduces a task-aware Mixture of Projectors (MoP) to align heterogeneous EEG features across different task families with the LLM embedding space. We further establish OneEEG-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating current MLLMs and our method on multi-task EEG understanding. Experiments show that existing MLLMs have limited ability to interpret EEG inputs, while OneEEG achieves stronger performance by integrating numerical and visual EEG representations with task-aware EEG-to-LLM projection. Extensive ablations and analyses further reveal the effects of visual EEG renderings, MoP variants, router behavior, and feature dispersion across EEG tasks.

title: Predicting Protein-Protein Interactions Using Vectorized Sequence Descriptors and Machine Learning Classifiers
desc: Accurate prediction of protein-protein interactions (PPIs) is fundamental for elucidating cellular mechanisms and accelerating drug discovery. Although experimental techniques provide extensive interaction maps, their high cost and time requirements necessitate robust computational alternatives. In this study, we present an interpretable machine-learning framework that integrates sequence-derived descriptors, specifically 120 Auto-Covariance (AC) features, 686 Conjoint Triad (CT) features, and 1,820 Local Descriptors (LD) features, with classical classification algorithms, including Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forests (RF), and XGBoost (XGB). Evaluated on a gold-standard sequence-based PPI benchmark dataset using stratified five-fold cross-validation, the models achieved robust classification accuracies: 86.92% (SVM), 97.75% (RF), and a peak cross-validation accuracy of 97.97% with XGBoost (Rec: 98.09%, Pr: 98.10%, F1: 98.09%). Furthermore, rigorous evaluation on an independent unseen (Human-PPI) test set demonstrated exceptional generalization capabilities. The Random Forest model emerged as the top-performing architecture, yielding an outstanding accuracy of 99.51%, a precision of 99.72%, a recall of 99.29%, an F1-score of 99.50%, an Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.9990, and an Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve (AUPRC) of 0.9989 (closely followed by XGBoost with 98.54% accuracy, AUROC 0.9979, and AUPRC 0.9974). Feature-importance analysis revealed that short-range physicochemical correlations (such as polarity and hydrophobicity lags in Protein 2), regional amino-acid compositions, and specific triad patterns (e.g., A/G/V-M/S/T/YM/S/T/Y) drive accurate PPI discrimination. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of domain-informed, handcrafted sequence features combined with machine-learning classifiers for PPI prediction, providing biologically interpretable insights with minimal computational overhead and enabling efficient, scalable interactome screening.

title: AI Is Already Inside the Doctor’s Visit. The Question Is Whether It’s Helping or Hunting for Billable Findings.
Artificial Intelligence in Acute Coronary Syndromes: From Early Diagnosis to Culprit Lesion Characterization, Coronary Physiology, and Risk Stratification.
desc: [Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland)] Artificial intelligence (AI) is being investigated across the acute coronary syndrome (ACS) care pathway, including early diagnosis, coronary lesion characterization, procedural guidance, and risk prediction. This comprehensive review examines the current evidence across the entire ACS trajectory, with particular emphasis on clinically actionable and interventional applications. AI-enabled electrocardiography (ECG) may improve detection of myocardial infarction, including occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI) that does not meet conventional STEMI criteria. Models combining clinical data and high-sensitivity troponin may improve early rule-out and rule-in. In coronary imaging, AI can quantify plaque characteristics and assist with the interpretation of OCT and IVUS, while image-derived physiology may help assess non-culprit lesions. However, better diagnostic accuracy does not necessarily translate into better revascularization decisions. AI-based models can also estimate post-ACS ischemic, bleeding, and mortality risk, although evidence that their use improves treatment or outcomes remains limited. The next priority is prospective evaluation of whether these tools improve decisions, workflow, and patient outcomes across diverse clinical settings.

title: Targeted Deep Regression - Initial Applications in Whole-Body Water-Fat MRI in UK Biobank
desc: UK Biobank is a British clinical study which, in addition to large amounts of medical data collected, plans to include detailed Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) examina- tions from 100,000 participants. The image data can be analyzed for example by auto- mated analysis with neural networks for image segmentation or classification to expand the collection of image-derived phenotypes for medical research. In this work, we pro- pose, present and evaluate a methodology that uses image-based regression to estimate numerical properties from the collected neck-to-knee water-fat MRI scans. It applies a ResNet50-style network to 2D multi-channel collages that represent targeted and study- specific anatomical sub-regions from the MRI scan. The targeted sub-region sampling is achieved by propagating manually defined subregions from a reference scan to the other >30,000 analyzed scans using image registration. The resulting collages can be compact while retaining high-resolution, for example by providing multiple slices of kidney tissue for a kidney volume regression network. This approach also enables group-wise saliency analysis that highlight image and anatomical regions used by the network for the pre- dictions. The method was applied for the regression endpoints of kidney volume, heart volume, and age. Predictive performance was found between R2 = 0.731-0.984 and the group-wise saliency maps were found to highlight medically relevant regions. We con- clude that the method can be used to standardize and restrict the information presented to a deep regression analysis pipeline, increasing information density and opening up a wide range of future medical inference studies.

title: How Much Can AI Virtual Cells Gain from Unified Perturbational Modeling?
desc: Predicting how individual cells respond to perturbations is a central task in artificial intelligence virtual cell (AIVC) modeling. However, integrating perturbation datasets is challenging because they differ in measured gene sets, perturbation types and cellular contexts. Existing AIVC predictors are typically developed for specific settings, limiting their applicability across heterogeneous datasets. Here, we investigate the extent to which AIVC predictors can benefit from unified perturbational modeling (UPM), a novel paradigm designed to integrate heterogeneous Perturb-seq datasets into a single predictive model. To this end, we introduce three unification modules into a variational autoencoder (VAE)-based AIVC predictor to address these sources of heterogeneity: gene-channel alignment, shared perturbation encoding, and joint embedding of gene expression and identity. We systematically evaluate and validate the individual contributions of these modules. Building on UPM, we assemble a dataset of 110 million cells spanning over 22,000 genes, four perturbation types and 76 cellular contexts, and use 89.7 million cells from 71 contexts to train a unified AIVC predictor with more than one billion parameters. Across genetic perturbation benchmarks, UPM achieves the highest PES and gene-wise response correlation among the evaluated models. It also improves all four evaluation metrics over State on the five held-out Tahoe-100M cell lines and over Stack on the cytokine benchmark. UPM also improves combinatorial perturbation prediction relative to specialized predictors. In the HSC application, our model achieves a 40.0% improvement in accuracy on a downstream task involving the recapitulation of effects induced by the knockdown of hepatic stellate cell (HSC)-related targets. Our implementation is openly available at https://github.com/youlab2025/UPM.

title: How Philips’ new AI officer sees it contending with the likes of ChatGPT
Review in coronary functional evaluation methods: applications of computational fluid dynamics and artificial intelligence in the context of coronary artery disease.
desc: [Frontiers in physiology] Coronary artery disease, driven by the progressive accumulation of atherosclerotic plaque within the epicardial coronary arteries, remains a leading cause of myocardial ischemia and global morbidity. A fundamental challenge in the clinical management of the disease has been the reliance on anatomic stenosis severity alone, a metric that frequently dissociates from the hemodynamic significance of a lesion and thus offers limited guidance for optimal revascularization. The advent of invasive measurements marked a transformative paradigm shift, enabling the development of a diverse functional indices for the evaluation of coronary physiology. Recently, the development of computational science and artificial intelligence has accelerated the translation of these physiological assessments into the non-invasive domain, primarily through high-fidelity numerical simulations and efficient machine learning algorithms. This review systematically examines the evolution of coronary functional assessment across several pivotal frontiers. It begins by contextualizing the diagnostic landscape prior to the widespread adoption of functional indices, where clinical decisions were predominantly informed by imaging-derived anatomical parameters. Subsequently, it traces the historical evolution of invasive coronary functional indices, critically evaluating the comparative effectiveness of pressure-derived metrics against flow-derived metrics in the detection of hemodynamically significant ischemia. Furthermore, a critical evaluation of emerging artificial intelligence methodologies for the non-invasive evaluation of functional significance were employed. By synthesizing these technological methodologies, this review aims to elucidate the appropriate clinical application of each functional index, thereby providing a road-map for clinicians to achieve precise, individualized ischemia evaluation and guide therapeutic decision-making in the contemporary era of precision cardiovascular medicine.

title: Low-rank MERA Decomposition of 3D OCT Image Volume for Compression, Denoising, Feature Extraction and Diagnosis of Retinal Diseases
desc: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) is a non-invasive imaging modality used for visualization of retinal tissue. However, OCT volumes are affected by speckle noise, which degrades image contrast and obscures fine structural details. Furthermore, modern clinical practice requires large field-of-view, high-resolution OCT volumes, whose storage and transmission are demanding for archiving and teleophthalmology applications. To address aforementioned challenges, we propose a low-rank multi-scale entanglement renormalization ansatz (MERA) tensor network approximation of 3D OCT image volume, where the image volume is represented as contractions of a top core factor encoding global features and multiple interacting low-rank orthogonal or semi-orthogonal factors modeling inter- and intra-B scan correlations. This representation jointly enables compression, denoising, and feature extraction. Unlike deep learning approaches, the proposed approach is training-free and processes each OCT volume independently. We evaluate the proposed framework on OCT image volumes acquired by two different scanners and demonstrate improved visual quality and reduced retinal layer segmentation errors in comparison with several competing methods. We also extract MERA features from two clinical OCT volume datasets. They are subsequently classified using a Grassmann-manifold nearest-subspace classifier. With the subspace dimension as its only hyperparameter, the classifier is theoretically shown to be robust in small-sample clinical scenario. We demonstrate competitive accuracy of classification of retinal diseases in these small-sample settings, where deep learning methods are often limited by the scarcity of labeled data. The proposed structure-aware model-driven representation learning for high-dimensional data under limited supervision provides good generalization performance while maintaining high interpretability.

title: ProtCell: a foundation model for single-cell proteomics
desc: Single-cell proteomics provides a direct functional readout of cellular states, but targeted assays measure limited and non-identical protein panels, fragmenting information across experiments. Here, we present ProtCell, a foundation model developed using approximately 380 million cells from 98 datasets for pretraining and evaluation. ProtCell combines protein-identity and continuous-abundance embeddings in a transformer encoder and learns cell- and protein-level representations through masked abundance modeling. ProtCell first connects fragmented profiles through transferable annotation and batch correction while preserving biological organization. It then extends limited profiles through abundance reconstruction and inference of an unmeasured cytotoxic protein program enriched in natural killer cells and memory CD8$^+$ T cells. The learned protein dependencies further guide the selection of compact panels that retain information for profile reconstruction and biological classification. ProtCell thus provides a framework for connecting fragmented proteomic profiles, extending information beyond measured panels and guiding more informative measurements.

title: From image biomarkers to treatment decisions: multimodal AI and clinical translation in gynecologic oncology.
desc: [Frontiers in oncology] Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly expanding across gynecologic oncology, but most applications remain focused on image interpretation and retrospective prediction rather than direct support of treatment decisions. This review examines how AI is progressing from imaging biomarkers toward multimodal decision-support systems that integrate radiologic, pathologic, molecular, and clinical information. We summarize current applications in ovarian, endometrial, and cervical cancers, with particular attention to preoperative risk stratification, surgical planning, radiotherapy, systemic treatment selection, treatment-response prediction, and multidisciplinary decision-making. Multimodal approaches are especially promising because they reflect the way clinical decisions are made and may provide greater value than models based on a single data source. However, the current evidence remains dominated by retrospective and often single-center studies, with limited external and prospective validation. Data heterogeneity, domain shift, incomplete multimodal datasets, bias, workflow integration, regulatory requirements, and model monitoring remain important barriers to routine implementation. We therefore outline a stepwise pathway for clinical translation, from robust multicenter validation and prospective human-AI evaluation to clinical-impact studies and post-deployment monitoring. The next phase of AI in gynecologic oncology should prioritize clinically meaningful decisions and measurable patient or workflow benefit rather than incremental gains in predictive performance alone.

title: Sequential versus fully conditional specification for tree-based synthesis of health data
desc: Disseminating synthetic data in place of original ones is a promising way to enforce privacy while complying with open science principles, especially in the healthcare domain. To keep pace with the rate at which researchers collect such data, there is a need for fast and flexible synthesis procedures. A popular class of such procedures is based on models of conditional distributions induced by decision trees. Such models can be combined into a synthetic distribution following two main approaches: sequential specification and fully conditional specification. However, there is currently no recommendation on which specification to use to optimize the risk-utility tradeoffs. In this work, we use both specifications to synthesize medical datasets by combining tree-based models of conditional distributions. We compare the quality of the resulting synthetic data using several metrics of risk and utility. Our results indicate no general superiority of either specification over the other. Sequential synthesis seems sensitive to the ordering of the variables, while the fully conditional specification involves more hyperparameters and incurs higher computational costs, which may limit its suitability for off-the-shelf synthesis procedures.

title: Identification of gene kinetics patterns improves RNA velocity and cell fate prediction using JuloVelo
desc: Single-cell RNA velocity has transformed our capacity to predict future cell states from sequencing snapshots, but existing methods rely on constant or binary kinetic assumptions that fail to capture the heterogeneous splicing dynamics of cellular differentiation. Here we present JuloVelo, a deep learning framework that demonstrates that identifying gene kinetics patterns to initialize neural network training dramatically improves RNA velocity model performance. By pre-determining whether each gene follows a Circle, Complete induction, or Complete repression pattern across cellular differentiation, JuloVelo initializes training with pattern-matched, pre-trained network weights, effectively guiding the cell-specific kinetics optimization away from biologically implausible parameter regimes. Additionally, JuloVelo demonstrates that multiome datasets can also be processed and modeled by utilizing promoter chromatin accessibility to guide kinetics pre-determination, and integrates an in silico perturbation framework to simulate transcription factor modulation on cell fate. Validated across eight datasets spanning erythrogenesis, neurogenesis, and endocrinogenesis, JuloVelo consistently outperformed constant-rate and cell-specific models, resolving the entire five-lineage differentiation program in hippocampal neurogenesis. Multiome processing improved both intrinsic and extrinsic velocity stability, and JuloVelo reduced computational execution time by approximately 70% compared to cellDancer. JuloVelo is available as an open-source package at https://github.com/jhlabtw/JuloVelo.jl.

title: Precision medicine for futile recanalization after mechanical thrombectomy in acute ischemic stroke: mechanisms, diagnostics, and tailored therapies.
desc: [Frontiers in neurology] Mechanical thrombectomy has substantially improved outcomes in appropriately selected patients with acute ischemic stroke, yet futile recanalization remains a major clinical challenge. Futile recanalization describes poor functional recovery despite technically successful macrovascular reperfusion, underscoring the incomplete relationship between angiographic reperfusion and tissue-level or microvascular perfusion. This narrative review summarizes current clinical, mechanistic, and translational evidence on the determinants of futile recanalization and evaluates emerging precision-medicine approaches to its prevention and management. Precision imaging has established a role in tissue-based patient selection, and recent randomized trials have expanded thrombectomy evidence to selected patients with large-core infarction. In contrast, current randomized evidence does not support routine endovascular treatment for unselected medium-vessel occlusion populations. We further examine bridging therapy versus direct mechanical thrombectomy, individualized periprocedural management, biomarkers, and decision support based on artificial intelligence. Clinical and imaging phenotypes may provide prognostic or mechanistic information, but no phenotype-based strategy has been prospectively validated to select bridging therapy or direct thrombectomy. Biomarkers currently remain primarily prognostic or exploratory. Artificial intelligence applications are largely focused on diagnostic and prognostic support. treatment-benefit prediction, by contrast, requires evidence of treatment-effect modification and prospective validation. Experimental studies of microvascular no-reflow and thrombo-inflammation provide biological rationale for targeted interventions but do not establish clinical efficacy. Future research should integrate multimodal imaging, biological profiling, and validated decision-support tools to move beyond angiographic success toward individualized strategies focused on tissue integrity and meaningful functional recovery.

title: Domain-Adapted Latent Diffusion Models for CT-to-PET Image Translation
desc: Positron Emission Tomography (PET) provides important metabolic information for tumor detection and staging but remains significantly less accessible than Computed Tomography (CT) due to its high cost, infrastructure requirements, and reliance on injected radioactive tracers. CT-to-PET image translation using generative models aims to address this disparity, yet state-of-the-art diffusion-based methods are limited by the scarcity of paired training data. To overcome this, we propose a domain-adapted latent diffusion framework that transfers natural-image priors using a relatively small dataset of 21,930 paired CT/PET slices, incorporating a signed power transform to resolve extreme intensity sparsity in PET data. Compared to CPDM, a state-ofthe-art baseline for CT-to-PET image translation, our approach yields superior performance in pixel-wise reconstruction and localized tumor fidelity, demonstrating effective transfer of natural-image priors to the medical domain. We further provide a systematic analysis of evaluation metric reliability for sparse PET data, showing that standard full-image metrics can be misleading indicators of translated image quality, and propose background-filtered and mask-restricted metrics as more clinically meaningful alternatives.

title: BLOOM: Biologically Informed Flow Matching for Transcriptomic Virtual Embryo Modeling
desc: Constructing a virtual embryo requires a generative representation of how heterogeneous cell populations change across developmental time. Here we introduce BLOOM, a biologically informed framework for conditional generation of developmental cell populations. BLOOM integrates temporal population context with developmental and regulatory priors through conditional flow matching to generate cell-expression distributions at queried stages in either temporal direction. Evaluation spans three mouse single-cell atlases covering prenatal development, visual-cortex maturation and multi-organ endothelial specialization. In comparisons with 22 time-series forecasting baselines, BLOOM ranks first for gene- and cell-expression correlations across all three datasets. Measured-stage evaluations support recovery of developmental expression patterns, population organization and marker-specific temporal relationships. Biological analyses connect these predictions to cell-state identities, gene programmes and regulatory associations. At unmeasured stages, interpolation and autoregressive history and future rollouts extend simulated expression dynamics between and beyond measured timepoints. Analyses of marker genes and temporal descriptors identify candidate differences in the timing of muscle-associated, neural and vascular-specialization programmes. Input-based gene perturbations further probe predicted responses of edited genes and associated molecular programmes across time. Together, BLOOM supports transcriptomic virtual embryo modeling by bridging temporal sampling gaps, exploring extended developmental trajectories and prioritizing gene-dependent hypotheses for experimental investigation.

title: From Isolated Intelligence to Interpretive Infrastructure in Radiology AI.
source: PubMed · The British journal of radiology
desc: [The British journal of radiology] Radiology has more regulatory-cleared artificial intelligence tools than any other medical specialty, yet they have delivered less consistent clinical impact than their benchmark performance suggested. We argue that the dominant response, scaling perceptual models and extending them toward autonomous agency, mistakes the nature of the problem. The limitation is architectural, not algorithmic: current systems perform isolated perception while remaining disconnected from the temporal, contextual, and experiential integration that interpretation requires. We trace this to a fundamental simulation gap, the absence of the counterfactual signal that lets AI reach superhuman performance in other domains, and argue that scaling alone cannot close it. In response, we outline a hybrid orchestration layer, grounded in established clinical frameworks, that assembles a comprehensive evidence base for the radiologist while keeping generative components constrained and interpretive judgment human. The shift is one of design paradigm: from isolated tools deployed alongside the radiologist to interpretive infrastructure that composes validated outputs into coherent evidence without anchoring the reader's own assessment.

title: Can JEV Support Clinical Trial Criteria Assessment?
desc: Clinical trial prescreening requires distinguishing unmet conditions from insufficient evidence in patient records. Given patient records, criterion questions, and predefined answer options, we retrospectively compared JEV, a non-generative decision model returning native option probabilities, with schema-constrained Qwen Flash across 2,048 test patient-condition pairs from TrialGPT and question-answer datasets derived from MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV, all evaluated under strict Zero Data Retention (ZDR) policies to ensure clinical data privacy. Both models assessed conditions individually or in batches sharing the same patient context, with performance measured against reference labels. In batch mode, JEV and Qwen achieved similar macro-F1 scores on TrialGPT (0.652 vs. 0.660) and MIMIC-IV (0.807 vs. 0.814), whereas JEV substantially outperformed Qwen on MIMIC-III (0.768 vs. 0.534; $Δ$ = +0.234, 95% CI: 0.187-0.281). This advantage largely reflected higher recall for conditions labeled as having insufficient information (56.3% vs. 9.9%). Across all three datasets, JEV also had lower observed median job latency (1.18-1.40 vs. 2.80-8.90 s) and 53%-74% lower estimated cost per condition. These findings position JEV as an initial assessment component that provides criterion-level judgments and flags potential information gaps for review. JEV's observed errors in interpreting clinical evidence underscore the need to verify its outputs against patient records before they inform eligibility decisions.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Peroral Cholangioscopy for the Diagnosis and Management of Biliary Strictures: Current Evidence and Future Directions.
desc: [Acta medica Okayama] Peroral cholangioscopy (POCS) enables direct intraductal visualization and targeted biopsies for indeterminate biliary strictures. However, its diagnostic performance remains operator-dependent and is limited by sampling error. As artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly advanced in gastrointestinal endoscopy, AI-assisted cholangioscopy has progressed from proof-of-concept image classification to multicenter validation, feature detection, and real-time application. Recent studies using digital single-operator cholangioscopy have reported diagnostic accuracy comparable to that of experts in differentiating malignant from benign strictures, and feature-based approaches can automatically detect tumor vessels and other key visual characteristics. Beyond classification, generative models may enhance mucosal and margin visualization through virtual chromoendoscopy, potentially improving lesion-margin assessment. Furthermore, new models compatible with multiple systems are emerging to address device heterogeneity, which is a key barrier to routine practice. This review summarizes the current evidence on AI-assisted POCS, discusses practical considerations for clinical translation, and highlights future directions, including real-time integration and multimodal decision support.

title: SAP-ViT: A Self-Attributing Patch Vision Transformer for Medical Image Classification
desc: Vision Transformer (ViT) classifiers commonly rely on a global classification (CLS) token for image-level prediction, which is poorly aligned with local interpretability requirements in medical imaging. We propose SAP-ViT, a Self-Attributing Patch Vision Transformer that replaces CLS-based classification with direct aggregation of last-layer patch embeddings. This design makes class predictions decomposable into patch-level contributions as part of the forward pass. To encourage concise and readable evidence, SAP-ViT applies sparsity regularization to the patch-weight distribution. Since self-attention mixes information across patch tokens, we further introduce an input-space back-mapping mechanism to estimate which input patches contribute to influential output patch embeddings. We evaluate SAP-ViT qualitatively and quantitatively on multiple medical image classification datasets spanning different imaging modalities. The results show that SAP-ViT maintains strong classification performance while providing consistent and interpretable patch-level explanations across datasets. Ablation results further show that both sparsity regularization and the alignment component of input-space back-mapping contribute to the final explanation quality. Overall, SAP-ViT provides a favorable trade-off between predictive accuracy and interpretability for ViT-based medical image classification.

title: Fusion of Deep Learning Radiomics and Clinical Features for Individualized Prediction of Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy Response in Osteosarcoma.
desc: [Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland)] Background: Stage IIB conventional osteosarcoma exhibits highly heterogeneous responses to neoadjuvant chemotherapy, necessitating reliable, noninvasive pre-treatment evaluation systems. Methods: This retrospective study of 198 patients utilized pre-treatment T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and baseline clinical data. Twelve classical convolutional neural network architectures were benchmarked to identify the optimal imaging backbone. This selected radiomics score was then integrated with core clinical variables using logistic regression to construct a multimodal model. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping++ (Grad-CAM++) and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) algorithms provided image- and feature-level interpretability. Results: DenseNet121 achieved the highest mean cross-validated area under the curve (AUC; 0.775) and was selected, with AUCs of 0.797 (95% CI: 0.716-0.877) and 0.701 (95% CI: 0.513-0.877) in the training and test cohorts. Adding the clinical variables improved discrimination, yielding a test-cohort AUC of 0.827 (95% CI: 0.661-0.992) with significant reclassification gain over the radiomics-only model (NRI = 1.28, IDI = 0.177; DeLong p = 0.011). Grad-CAM++ activation concentrated on the solid medullary and extraosseous soft-tissue components, and SHAP ranked the radiomics score as the strongest contributor. Conclusions: Integrating deep learning radiomics with key clinical features provides a noninvasive tool for the individualized prediction of neoadjuvant chemosensitivity in osteosarcoma.

title: EXCISE: Locating and Excising Distracting Sentences in Medical Question Answering
desc: Language models are increasingly considered for clinical decision support, where their answers should be grounded in clinical evidence and remain robust to irrelevant information. Prior work shows that a single irrelevant sentence can lower the accuracy of medical models, but not where inside the model its effect can be removed, or how to do so without knowing which sentence it is. We find that blocking attention to a known distractor restores the answer, whereas head masking can suppress correct answers. We also show that the model's hidden states mark the distractor as the sentence that least fits the case even when the model follows it. To remove a distractor's effect without knowing which sentence it is, we propose EXCISE, an inference-time method that blocks the sentence most influencing the answer, but only if the model's hidden states mark it as inconsistent with the case. On MedQA-TD (MedQA with Targeted Distractors), a benchmark we construct in which each distractor targets a specific wrong option, EXCISE gains 16.7-22.8 accuracy points at a 1.5-2.1-point cost on the same questions without distractors, outperforming prompting, rewriting, and steering baselines for all three models. Its gains extend to MedDistractQA and BiasMedQA, as well as chain-of-thought generation.

title: Evaluation of Large Language Model Concordance With AAOS Clinical Practice Guidelines for Carpal Tunnel Syndrome.
desc: [Hand (New York, N.Y.)] Large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and Mistral are increasingly used to obtain medical information, but their accuracy in carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) management is uncertain. This study evaluated whether LLM-generated recommendations align with American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons (AAOS) clinical practice guidelines (CPGs). Four LLMs (ChatGPT-4, Gemini, Claude-3, Mistral-7B) were queried with standardized prompts derived from AAOS CTS CPGs. Each prompt was asked 3 times per model, and responses were synthesized. Two blinded reviewers graded outputs as concordant, discordant, or indeterminate, with disagreements resolved by consensus. Concordance distributions were compared using χ2 testing with Bonferroni correction. Inter-rater reliability was measured with Cohen's κ. Across 252 recommendations, 72.6% were concordant, 11.5% discordant, and 15.9% indeterminate. ChatGPT achieved the highest concordance (92.1%) and lowest discordance (1.6%), while Mistral performed poorest (52.4% concordance, 17.5% discordance). Reviewer agreement was excellent (κ = 0.91). Over 1 in 4 LLM-generated CTS recommendations were not concordant with AAOS CPGs. ChatGPT outperformed other models, though variable performance underscores the need for clinician oversight and careful validation before clinical use.

title: TransECG-SSL: Hybrid Self-Supervised Representation Learning for ECG Arrhythmia Classification
desc: Cross-dataset generalisation remains a major challenge for automated electrocardiogram (ECG) arrhythmia classification because of differences in patient populations, acquisition protocols, annotation practices, and class distributions. Learning representations that remain informative across independent datasets could reduce reliance on dataset-specific labelled data. We propose TransECG-SSL, a self-supervised framework for transferable heartbeat representation learning from unlabelled ECG data. A Transformer encoder is pretrained using a hybrid objective combining masked signal reconstruction and contrastive learning, then frozen and evaluated by linear probing under patient-disjoint evaluation. Experiments across three public ECG databases and seven source--target settings show that Hybrid SSL consistently outperforms randomly initialised Transformers and achieves higher balanced accuracy than architecture-matched source-supervised pretraining. Reconstruction-only SSL remains competitive with Hybrid SSL, whereas contrastive-only pretraining performs substantially worse, highlighting the importance of masked reconstruction for transferability. Cross-dataset transfer nevertheless reduces balanced accuracy relative to target-specific self-supervised pretraining, while minority arrhythmia classes remain challenging under severe class imbalance. These findings demonstrate the potential of label-efficient self-supervised learning for cross-dataset ECG representation transfer while highlighting persistent limitations from domain shift and class imbalance.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Molecular Imprinting for Efficient Polymer Design and Enhanced Liquid-Phase Separation.
desc: [Electrophoresis] Molecularly imprinted polymers (MIPs) have become significantly more desirable as synthetic polymers with recognition sites designed for target molecules for use in liquid-phase separation due to their high selectivity, stability, and robustness. However, the development of MIPs remains challenging, as the selection of functional monomers, cross-linkers, pore-forming agents, and polymerization conditions often relies on labor-intensive experimental trial-and-error methods. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and silica computational tools have presented new opportunities to accelerate the rational design and optimization of MIPs by enabling data-driven prediction and decision-making. The integration of AI and ML with MIP technology and liquid chromatography (LC) enables the development of highly selective separation materials. These combined approaches support real-time analysis and adaptive process control, driving progress towards fully autonomous analytical systems. ML algorithms, including artificial neural network (ANN), support vector machines, random forests (RF), and gradient boosting models, have been successfully applied to predict adsorption capacity, imprinting factor, binding affinity, and synthesis performance. In parallel, computational techniques such as molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations have enabled the understanding of molecular recognition mechanisms. Furthermore, AI tools have further facilitated more rational and systematic selection of imprinting components. Beyond materials design, AI is increasingly integrated into liquid-phase separation technologies through quantitative structure-retention relationship (QSRR) models, Bayesian optimization, and reinforcement learning. These approaches enable automated retention time predictions, chromatographic method optimization, and intelligent data analysis. This review comprehensively addresses the latest developments published between 2018 and 2025, with particular focus on recent developments that reflect the rapidly evolving intersection of AI/ML in MIP technology and liquid-phase separation.

title: Synthetic Deformable Tubular Benchmark: A mechanically annotated dataset for evaluating deformable 3D reconstruction
desc: Evaluating deformable 3D reconstruction requires ground truth linking camera motion, surface deformation, material correspondence and image appearance. We introduce the Synthetic Deformable Tubular Benchmark, generated with LumenMorph, an open-source toolkit for creating, annotating and evaluating tubular scenes. The release contains 5,580 RGB images. Its baseline crosses three surface-motion conditions with moving and stationary cameras in six scene families; matched appearance variants cover only moving-camera finite-element actions in four families. Documented public and evaluation interfaces expose camera poses, geometry, depth, deformation fields, persistent material correspondences and discrete finite-element records. Persistent triangle identities and material weights let users track the same surface location across frames and query its three-dimensional trajectory. Separately implemented geometric and mechanical checks assess annotation consistency with the generating models. Structure-from-motion, optical-flow and supplied-geometry displacement-interpolation studies demonstrate how the resource distinguishes registration coverage from geometric accuracy, exposes camera- and surface-motion effects, and tests the benefits and mismatch of mechanical priors. Public readers, evaluation contracts and the configurable generator support reuse and extension. Data integrity, fixed-environment repeatability and retained-prediction score replay have distinct verification scopes. The benchmark provides a controlled synthetic reference without claiming anatomical or clinical realism.

title: Demystifying Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Health care: Is AI Friend or Foe?
desc: [Professional case management] The literature review is saturated with positive tones about the use of AI not only in health care but also in all aspects of our daily lives as well. The positivity range is extensive, ranging from increased accuracy, efficiency, productivity, profitability to creativity, equity, and advancement. Yet, the public is circumspect with continual exposure to news about cybersecurity threats or attacks, identity theft, violations of privacy, and challenges of establishing trust in their daily encounters with technology amidst prevalence of deep fakes, voice cloning, and AI-generated images or videos of people. A meta-synthesis of AI-related literature inclusive of expert panels is examined as an exploratory search for AI applicability and use in the health care landscape. The purpose of this article is to demystify AI highlighting areas of its use in health care, ways for clinicians specifically, care managers to bridge that divide and ascertain key practice standards with emphasis on its ethical use in health care. The settings using AI that were considered in this article include Health plans, Hospitals, medical practices or clinics, and Hospitals' Revenue Cycle Management (RCM). Implications and recommendations for case management engagement in AI are addressed relative to the standards of practice (SOPs).

title: O2D-MedNet: An Optimization-Aware Dual-Domain Framework for Robust Medical Image Segmentation
desc: Medical image segmentation (MIS) remains challenging due to composite degradations and multi-scale geometric variations, which jointly impair lesion-background separability, structural consistency, and optimization stability. Existing single-stream frameworks entangle heterogeneous cues within a single representation pathway, while hybrid-stream approaches often rely on generic or static fusion, limiting effective coordination across domains and failing to explicitly address optimization instability. To overcome these limitations, we propose a new optimization-aware dual-domain framework for MIS (O2D-MedNet). First, a degradation-aware dualdomain interaction (DDI) module integrates Fourier - and Wavelet-domain features to suppress degradation-sensitive responses while preserving structural and fine-detail information. Second, a cross-backbone contour-guided fusion (CGF) module enables selective interaction between CNN-based local detail modeling and visual state-space-based global structure modeling, improving boundary accuracy and representation consistency. Third, a gradient-context optimization (GCO) strategy stabilizes training by adaptively adjusting learning dynamics based on loss trends and gradient statistics, mitigating instability caused by class imbalance and heterogeneous sample difficulty. Extensive experiments on six benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art MIS methods across multiple imaging modalities. Further analyses confirm enhanced sensitivity, structural consistency, and optimization stability, validating the effectiveness of the proposed O2D-MedNet for robust MIS under heterogeneous conditions.

title: Accuracy of deep learning in quantifying epicardial adipose tissue: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
desc: [Internal and emergency medicine] Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) is significantly associated with cardiovascular disease and poor prognosis. Deep learning (DL) models have been explored for automatic EAT segmentation, but systematic evidence verifying their effectiveness is currently lacking. We conducted this meta-analysis to evaluate the accuracy of DL models for EAT segmentation and quantification, aiming to support the development of automated tools. We searched the Cochrane Library, Embase, Web of Science, PubMed, and IEEE Xplore through February 20, 2026. Studies reporting DL-based quantitative EAT segmentation were included. Quality was assessed with QUADAS-2. The Dice similarity coefficient (Dice), correlation coefficient (R), and Bland-Altman bias were used to evaluate segmentation efficacy, the correlation between automated segmentation and reference standards, and consistency, respectively. A random-effects model with the Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman method pooled these measures. Thirty eligible studies were included, covering five image types. For non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT), the pooled Dice was 0.888 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.853-0.924), and the pooled R reached 0.973 (95%CI: 0.958-0.982). The contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) subgroup performed best, yielding a Dice of 0.910 (95% CI: 0.881-0.939) and an R of 0.989 (95% CI: 0.976-0.995). This meta-analysis quantifies the accuracy of DL models for EAT segmentation and volume quantification. The findings indicate that DL achieves robust accuracy on both NCCT and CECT images. However, given that most current studies rely on internal validation, future work should prioritize large-scale, multicenter external validation to support the translation of these promising DL tools into robust clinical diagnostic systems.

title: High Scores, Hidden Failures: Evaluating Codebook-Based LLM Content Analysis
desc: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for codebook-based content analysis in computational social science, where codebooks translate theoretical concepts into labeling schemes. While prior work reports strong predictive performance, it remains unclear whether these systems produce reliable and robust text annotations. We conduct a large-scale empirical failure-mode analysis of LLM-based coding pipelines across four datasets and five models by systematically evaluating their stability, robustness, and conceptual validity under controlled perturbations, domain shifts, and optimization procedures. We uncover multiple failure modes that are largely invisible under standard metrics, showing that high aggregate scores frequently coexist with severe label-level disparities, instability across runs, domain sensitivity, and shifts in label interpretation. Importantly, these failure modes persist under widely used optimization strategies and remain largely invisible under standard metrics such as accuracy and micro-F1. Our results demonstrate that current LLM-based coding pipelines cannot be treated as stable measurement tools without targeted validation beyond aggregate performance.

title: An Integrated Artificial Intelligence Framework for Nanomedicine Engineering.
desc: [Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany)] The translation of nanomedicines is frequently bottlenecked by trial-and-error optimization. Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) transforms this process into a closed-loop, experimentally grounded discovery ecosystem. This Review provides a roadmap for this paradigm, demonstrating how AI, high-throughput testing, and nanoscale design converge to generate clinically translatable nanotherapeutics. We emphasize the necessity of standardized multimodal data-spanning pharmacokinetic, biodistribution, and drug-release profiles-anchored strictly to validated biological phenomena. Furthermore, we evaluate an algorithmic spectrum, ranging from classical machine learning to physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) and reinforcement learning (RL), to align models with specific formulation objectives. To bridge computational design and empirical reality, we examine how high-throughput technologies, such as robotic laboratories and in vivo DNA-barcoding multiplexing, operationalize the "Design-Make-Test-Analyze" (DMTA) cycle for dynamic model recalibration. Ultimately, this review demonstrates how integrating AI, physical constraints, and automated validation accelerates the rational design of next-generation nanomedicines.

title: Transglycosidases from aspergillus genus and their applications in food processing: Advances in enzyme mining and smart biocatalysis.
source: PubMed · International journal of biological macromolecules
desc: [International journal of biological macromolecules] Transglycosidases (TGs) constitute a family of glycoside hydrolases that perform glycosyl transfer via intra- and intermolecular substitution. A. niger, A. oryzae, and other Aspergillus strains represent the major industrial sources of TGs, which are widely applied in food processing. However, prominent bottlenecks still restrict the optimization of enzyme performance, industrial adaptation, and the construction of synergistic catalytic systems. This comprehensive review expounds the application potential of Aspergillus-derived TGs in food processing, analyzes the scientific basis of artificial intelligence (AI) regulation on enzyme catalytic performance, systematically summarizes the molecular modification and multi-enzyme synergistic mechanisms, and illustrates their application effects in the fields of prebiotic oligosaccharides, dairy products, brewing, and baking. Furthermore, it promotes the in-depth integration of AI and food biomanufacturing, and advances the high-quality development of the green functional food processing industry, showing sustainable and bright prospects in smart bioprocessing and big-health food research.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Nanobody Engineering for Pathogen Recognition: From Functional Epitope Prioritization to Multimodal Foundation Models.
desc: [Biomolecules] Nanobodies are compact and stable proteins derived from the variable domain of camelid heavy-chain-only antibodies (VHH). Advances in structural biology, molecular modeling, and artificial intelligence (AI) are shifting VHH discovery from empirical selection toward data-driven design. However, predicted binding alone does not ensure biological activity or successful translation, particularly for antigenically variable pathogens. Complementing recent reviews that broadly survey computational VHH modeling and optimization, this review focuses on how antigen biology and functional epitope prioritization can guide the design of pathogen-targeting VHHs. We organize the field along a structure-function-translation continuum, connecting the structural basis of VHH recognition and available data resources with conventional discovery, antigen-guided de novo design, and sequence-structure learning. We further examine how developability, recombinant production, multispecificity, humanization, structural dynamics, and antigenic variation shape the progression from predicted binders to functional VHHs. Finally, we discuss how multimodal foundation models could integrate these dimensions to support the design of functional, manufacturable, and escape-resilient VHHs.

title: The psychology of learning with generative AI in foreign language education: building a theory of metacognition, trust, and human-AI co-regulation through a systematic review.
desc: [Frontiers in psychology] Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is reshaping foreign language education, yet the psychological processes underlying effective learner-AI interaction remain fragmented. This theory-building systematic review synthesizes empirical evidence on metacognition, trust, and human-AI co-regulation in GenAI-supported foreign language learning. Following PRISMA 2020 procedures, web of science and Scopus were searched for studies published from 2022 to June 2026. After screening, 51 empirical studies were included. The findings show that metacognition shapes learners' planning, monitoring, regulation, and reflection; trust influences how learners accept, verify, modify, or reject AI-generated information and feedback; and human-AI co-regulation involves the dynamic distribution of cognitive and regulatory activity between learners and GenAI within teacher-mediated instructional contexts. AI literacy and learner agency further support critical evaluation, strategic AI use, and retention of human decision-making responsibility. Based on these findings, the review develops the metacognition-trust-co-regulation (MTC) framework, which conceptualizes effective GenAI-assisted learning as an iterative process in which metacognitive regulation informs trust, trust calibrates reliance, and reliance shapes human-AI co-regulation. The framework positions GenAI as a cognitive partner whose educational value depends on critically informed, metacognitively regulated, and humanly governed use.

title: Design and Experimental Validation of an Embedded Edge Artificial Intelligence Camera System for Real-Time Intelligent Vision.
desc: [Sensors (Basel, Switzerland)] This study presents the design and experimental validation of an embedded edge artificial intelligence (AI) camera system for intelligent vision applications. The developed system integrates a multicore edge computing processor and a dedicated AI engine into a compact smart camera platform, enabling on-device image processing, intelligent recognition, and localized decision-making. The hardware implementation incorporates circuit design, impedance-controlled high-speed signal routing, and printed circuit board (PCB) stack-up design. The signal integrity of the MIPI Display Serial Interface (MIPI-DSI) is evaluated through scattering-parameter simulations and measurements, while the conducted radio frequency (RF) transmitter performance and radiated emissions of the fabricated prototype are experimentally assessed. In an outdoor and indoor parking-lot field test, the integrated system processed images at approximately 2 frames per second (FPS) while operating in multi-task mode at an image resolution of 1280 × 960 pixels. When configured exclusively for license plate recognition, the system achieves a processing throughput of up to 45 FPS. For all 13 tested vehicles, comprising two buses, two trucks, and nine cars, both the predicted vehicle type and complete license plate number matched the ground truth, yielding an integrated recognition accuracy of 12/13 for this test sample. Representative measurements of the prototype's DC input power were approximately 2.20-6.32 W at a supply voltage of 12 V. These results demonstrate the feasibility of the developed edge AI camera for fixed-location parking-management applications and real-time edge inference capability.

title: Millet fermentations: a review on microorganisms, fermentation parameters, nutrients bio-utilization, and future prospects.
desc: [Frontiers in microbiology] Millets are prominent cereal materials worldwide. Fermentation is a typical bioprocessing method of millets, which boosts the sensory properties, nutritional composition and biological activity of millet products. In recent years, millets fermentation has been receiving increasing attention and many cutting-edge technologies have demonstrated significant application potential. This review provides an overview of recent progress in millets fermentation. The fermentation pattern, fermentation microorganisms, as well as process parameters are recognized as key factors that affect the fermentation process and product quality. Meanwhile, fermentation improves the bio-utilization of millet nutrients from aspects such as reducing starch digestibility, promoting the release and transformation of polyphenols, and increasing the bioaccessibility of minerals. Application of omics integration strategies, artificial intelligence models and online detection techniques exhibits great potential in exploring the fermentation mechanism and enhancing the fermentation efficiency and stability. These advancements are poised to significantly enhance industrial fermentation practices and highlights the value of fermented millets in healthy diets.

title: Artificial Intelligence as a Tool for Combating Antimicrobial Resistance.
desc: [Microorganisms] Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has evolved from a looming concern into a fully realized global emergency, reshaping clinical practice and public health faster than the adaption abilities of our traditional countermeasures [...].

title: Putting Large Language Models into Environmental Context.
desc: [Environmental science & technology] The emergence of large language models (LLMs) has fundamentally transformed information interaction, yet their application in environmental science and engineering (ESE) is hindered by multimodal data formats, dynamic context requirements, and hallucination risks. To transition from general-purpose models to domain expert agentic systems, this Perspective introduces a three-pillar framework for ESE-LLMs: domain perception, knowledge grounding, and action capability. Implementing these capabilities introduces potential pitfalls such as geographic representation bias, catastrophic forgetting, and source authenticity vulnerabilities, which require strategic model blending and careful data curation to overcome. Furthermore, rigorous evaluation must extend beyond standard knowledge benchmarks to systematically assess factuality, fairness, consistency, and safety using both human and automated metrics. Finally, we present a decision-guided deployment workflow that helps researchers in ESE fields integrate LLMs into their workflow. Ultimately, achieving trustworthy environmental intelligence relies on continuous evaluation, robust governance, and sustained interdisciplinary collaboration to safely deploy agentic ESE-LLMs for high-stakes environmental challenges.
